renders._yaml:
- component: card
  title: Pseudoaligned reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average share of reads that kallisto pseudoaligns to the transcriptome, and the box shows the quartiles over samples. It answers how much of the sequencing the reference explains.
    How to read: a high share means the reads match the reference. A low share points to a wrong or incomplete reference, a wrong chemistry or poor-quality reads, so check the index and the technology setting first.
    Note: kallisto and bustools publish no pass mark for this share, so none is drawn.
  column: p_pseudoaligned
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: average share, with quartiles
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Cells called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of cells called per sample after the bustools filter, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how many cells each sample yields.
    How to read: compare it with the cell count you loaded. Far fewer cells point to a stringent filter or a failed capture, and far more to ambient RNA called as cells.
  column: cells_called
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with quartiles

- component: card
  title: Barcodes on the whitelist
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of barcodes found on the technology whitelist after correction, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how many distinct barcodes the reads carry, including empty droplets.
    How to read: this is far larger than the called cells, because most barcodes are empty droplets or ambient RNA. A sample whose count is out of line with its peers deserves a look at its input reads.
  column: n_barcodes
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with quartiles

- component: table
  title: Run metrics
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with the reads processed and pseudoaligned, the pseudoaligned share, the barcodes on the whitelist and the cells called by the filter. It answers the exact numbers behind the cards.
    How to read: compare the pseudoaligned share across samples to find one that differs, then read its barcode and cell counts.
